date_evidence: Council of the EU PRESS EN PRESS RELEASE 299/26 07/05/2026 - Artificial Intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline rules

HTML and PDF pages render via client-side scripts so the body could not be fetched as text; date taken from the verbatim Council press-release reference '299/26 07/05/2026' returned in search results (PDF dateline), corroborated across multiple legal trackers and the European Commission release IP/26/1024. topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: Robot Density Surges in Europe, Asia, and Americas
date_evidence: Frankfurt, Apr 08, 2026 - Economies worldwide are prioritising the integration of factory robots, as automation becomes a critical tool for boosting productivity.
key_claim: Global manufacturing robot density reached new records in 2024 - Western Europe 267, North America 204 and Asia 131 robots per 10,000 employees - with Asia's density up 11% and China's up 17% year-on-year, evidencing sustained acceleration in factory-floor automation intensity.
signals_supported: robot density rising / automation intensity accelerating
verbatim_quote: The Western European countries reached a record 267 robots per 10,000 employees in the manufacturing industry 2024 - ahead of North America with 204 units and Asia with 131 units.
notes: Tier 2: IFR is the authoritative industry body for robotics statistics. This April 2026 press release presents a fresh cut of World Robotics 2025 data, with growth rates that let momentum be read by region.

topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: China Makes AI-powered Robots Core of National Strategy
date_evidence: Frankfurt, May 05, 2026 - China has launched its 15th Five-Year Plan by placing robotics at the heart of its modern industrial system.
key_claim: China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) places AI-integrated robotics at the centre of its industrial strategy, with domestic suppliers' share of China's industrial-robot installations rising from 30% in 2020 to 57% in 2024 - a fast-accelerating localisation and policy-push signal.

notes: Tier 2: IFR industry-body analysis of Chinese national policy. topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: From pilots to performance: How COOs can scale AI in manufacturing
date_evidence: December 15, 2025 | Article ... A new survey of manufacturing COOs shows high hopes for scaling AI—and high budgets.
key_claim: A McKinsey survey of 101 manufacturing COOs (June-July 2025) found ~93% plan to raise digital/AI spend yet about two-thirds of manufacturers are still only at the exploration or targeted-implementation stage and just 2% have AI fully embedded across operations – evidence that industrial-AI ambition is Accelerating while actual scaled deployment is Stable/stalled.
signals_supported: gap between AI investment and scaled value
notes: Tier 2: major-consultancy primary survey research. Core counter-evidence source – quantifies the 'pilot purgatory' problem and the underinvestment in enablers (workforce, IT/OT, cybersecurity) that keeps deployments stuck.
verbatim_quote: About two-thirds of respondents indicate that their companies' AI implementation is still at the exploration or targeted-implementation stage. A mere 2 percent say that AI is now fully embedded across all operations.

topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: Will Robotics Have a ChatGPT Moment?
key_claim: Agility Robotics co-founder Jonathan Hurst and former Google X Everyday Robots lead Hans Peter Brøndmo argue there will be no single breakthrough 'ChatGPT moment' for robotics – a real YouTube-to-reality gap, an unsolved data problem and immature force-compliant actuators mean AI-powered factory robots will deliver value only incrementally, task by task.
signals_supported: robotics foundation models / agentic AI maturity
notes: Tier 3: flagship engineering-press opinion piece by senior practitioners; informed insider counter-evidence tempering humanoid/physical-AI momentum. Most-recent-30-day window. Opinion format, so claims framed as expert assessment rather than data.
verbatim_quote: We believe AI will enable an inflection point in robotics advances, but that it will be through the well-engineered application of coordinated systems of different AI tools rather than a single ChatGPT-style breakthrough.

signals_supported: agentic / VLA industrial AI moving to commercial execution

topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: Factory Paying Human Worker to Watch Robot Worker All Day
key_claim: At Schaeffler's Cheraw, South Carolina plant an Agility Robotics Digit humanoid works an eight-hour shift operating a stamping press – but only inside a plexiglass cage watched by a human Agility contractor, because the robot still cannot detect people, and Agility's ~$10-$25/hour cost remains above the plant's $20/hour entry wage.
notes: Tier 3: quality tech journalism reporting on Wall Street Journal on-site coverage. Counter-evidence on deployment friction – shows real humanoid deployments are still caged, supervised and not yet cost-competitive, a Stable-with-caveats rather than breakout signal.
verbatim_quote: Digit, the WSJ explains, can’t detect human beings in its environment just yet, requiring it to be penned off due to machine-guarding regulations.

topic: Advanced Manufacturing Automation and Industrial AI
title: America Is Building Factories. So Where Are the Jobs?
key_claim: Despite roughly $1.595 trillion of committed US manufacturing investment, net factory employment was down about 82,000 jobs from January 2025 to early 2026 – a lag the article attributes to multi-year build timelines and automation, with 88% of 2024 reshored roles classed high- or medium-high-tech, signalling that reshoring momentum is not translating into headcount.
notes: Tier 3: industrial trade publication; analytical piece sourced to BLS/FRED, Census Bureau and the Reshoring Initiative. Shows reshoring capital Accelerating while factory employment is Stable-to-Fading – the workforce counter-narrative a momentum tracker needs.
verbatim_quote: $1.595 trillion in manufacturing investment has been committed. Net factory jobs since January 2025 are down 82,000. Both of those things are true.
